summary: A study found family dinners with mixed politics ended much sooner than those with matching politics.
realLife: A 2018 study in Science found that families with mixed politics spent 20 to 50 minutes less at the Thanksgiving table than matched groups. The effect was about three times stronger in areas with heavy political advertising. Partisans of one side left earlier, and the other side was more likely to skip the gathering entirely.
